EventName: Indy Cycloplex Short Track Mountain Bike Series 2026
EventNotes:
Indy Cycloplex Short Track Cross Country Mountain Bike Racing 

ICX STXC is a new Short Track Racing Series taking place at the Indy Cycloplex. Aiming to bring MTB racing to the City of Indianapolis, this STXC race series serves as a training/development series for racers to hone their MTB skills. The STXC series will also take place on Marque Race Nights at the Indy Cycloplex, with racing taking place on the Velodrome and BMX track too. Food, Beverages, and Music will be available for all to enjoy during Marquee Race Nights at ICX!

The goal: Provide STXC MTB racing for the greater Indianapolis cycling community.

This series is inclusive of all ability levels and will allow riders to self-select categories independent of USA Cycling categories to provide a chance to race against groups that are similar in skillset and fitness levels. Juniors to Masters, Collegiate and Elite, Men and Women, all are encouraged to race in the wave that presents them the best fit.

Race Day Schedule: (will be the same for all race days)


6:00pm – Junior Men and Women
This is for juniors dipping their toes into STXC racing for
the first time.

These results will be posted at the Indy Cycloplex and on the Indy Cycloplex Website but will not be posted to USA Cycling's website. 

 

6:30pm – Intermediate Men and Women
This is for racers that have some STXC experience and looking for a little challenge. Also for 14–17-year-old juniors that are looking to challenge themselves, Collegiate B’s and C's, and racers that aspire to earn upgrade points for USAC categories

These results will be posted at the Indy Cycloplex and on the Indy Cycloplex Website and will be posted to USA Cycling's website. 

 

7:00pm – Elite Men and Women
This is the fastest field of the evening. Local Pros and the top collegiate riders will race in this category. High level juniors and u23 riders should race in this category, as well as anyone else that is looking for a leg busting challenge on a Thursday night.

These results will be posted at the Indy Cycloplex and on the Indy Cycloplex Website and will be posted to USA Cycling's website. 

 

The course:

Utilizing the infamous Indy Cycloplex “Mountain” (ok, hill!) next to Cold Springs Road, the ICX STXC course will vary from week to week. The starting grid and finish line will be placed in the parking lot of the ICX, and racing will take place on and around the hillside utilizing some of the single-track MTB trails at ICX. Course direction will change from event to event, and different features will be included or removed for each event night as well. All STXC courses will NOT utilize the DS course at ICX, these STXC events are geared toward high intensity single track style MTB racing.

All times EST - Held under USAC permit #10515

• Promoter reserves right to modify schedule, race lengths, and categories.

• Day-of registration late fee on BikeReg: $10

Sometimes you need a Big Awesome Goal to get motivated – and this series fits the bill. 

The Hotter'N Hell Hundred can be a very challenging ride with wind, heat and hills on all of their routes. Through the years I have noticed that the people who handle these challenges the best are the people who are out cycling in area rides leading up to the HHH. This little lesson motivated me to put together a ride series that would help you get ready for the BIG ride in Wichita Falls.

The Road to Hotter’N Hell is a bundle of 5 small community bike rides (one each month, starting in April) plus the Hotter’N Hell. Each ride in our series features challenging routes and a variety of distances blended with Texas Hospitality. We’ve ridden these rides for decades and know that they are all committed to providing an excellent ride experience. Here’s how it works.

When you register for the RTHH you are automatically registered for all 6 of our featured rides (we also offer bundles of 3, 4 or 5 rides). Single registrations are available (no tandem registration rate is available). Your bundle also includes the FREE ride T-shirts (Tour de Cypress, Possum Pedal, Peach Pedal and the Hotter'N Hell) . You will also have the option to include a T-shirt from the Head for the Hills (additional fee of $7) or Blazin' Saddle 75 (additional fee of $5).

When registering, you have 3 options: 

Just Rides (ride bundle with no apparel)

Rides & Socks (ride bundle with a pair of custom socks)

Rides & Jersey (ride bundle with a custom jersey)

After you register for a ride bundle that includes apparel, you will receive instructions for ordering your socks OR  your jersey.

You'll have opportunities to pick up your socks at each of our rides. Shipping is included with the jersey. 

Each ride will send you a confirmation (in April) so that you can get your packet, t-shirt and other goodies before the ride or on the day of the ride. Here are our featured rides and their scheduled dates:

Tour de Cypress                April 18, 2026            Mt. Vernon, TX                           Routes of 10, 30, 45, 52 and 62 miles

Peach Pedal                       July 11, 2026               Weatherford, TX                        Routes of 8, 28, 38 and 60 miles

Blazin’ Saddle 75             August 1, 2026            Granbury, TX                               Routes of 20, 40, 62 and 75 miles

Hotter’N Hell                   August 29, 2026          Wichita Falls, TX                           Routes of 10k, 25, 50, 62, 75 and 100 miles

The 11th Annual Rose Mountain Rumble (RMR) takes place Saturday, August 29th, 2026. 

Registration opens 7:00 AM, rolling starts begin 7:30 AM.

The RMR is a non-timed gravel ride that tours the scenic dirt roads of Lyndeborough, New Hampshire and surrounding towns. We welcome riders of every ability and offer a variety of route options from a 25-miler for more casual riders, an intermediate 45-miler, to 66 and 80-mile courses that challenge the most competitive gravel grinder.  The RMR is capped at 150 riders.  

All the routes begin and end at Lyndeborough's historic Center Hall.   The 25-mile course is marked, while the 45, 66 and 80-mile courses are not.  Riders need to be prepared to follow provided cue sheets and are strongly encouraged to download the supplied GPX courses ahead of time which can be found at www.rosemountainrumble.com on the Courses page.  

Registration includes water/snack stops, a delicious post-ride lunch provided by the Wilton-Lyndeborough Women’s Club, and a tee-shirt custom-designed each year by local bike builder and graphic artist Kris Henry.  Net proceeds benefit the Piscataquog Land Conservancy, a regional land trust that has been protecting open space in southern New Hampshire since 1970.

We are holding the 2026 registration fee level with last year at $125 per rider.  To help younger riders be part of the Rumble, we are continuing our discounted registration fee for riders 18 and under.  Just contact us and we'll send you a discount code to use at checkout.

We can't wait to see you…get ready to rumble!  - Team RMR

We are crushed to announce that we have made the difficult decision to cancel Barn Gravel for 2026 due to low registration numbers, life circumstances, the economy, and permit requirements.

Although the formal event has been canceled, we would still love to bring the community together. Aaron Johnson and GO GRAVA plan to host an informal social ride using a shorter version of the Barn Gravel route—approximately 40 miles.

Date: 29 August
Gather time: 9:00 AM
Location: GO GRAVA Bicycles
840 N Park Road
Wyomissing, PA

Aaron will email additional information later this week, including the route and important ride details. Please note that this will be a community ride rather than a permitted Barn Gravel event. Sign up for the Go Grava email notification at https://gograva.com/pages/wednesday-night-ride under "Join the Squad". 

They will also be collecting donations that day for Helping Harvest, with the goal of bringing this year's donation to at least $1,000.

What is the future of Barn Gravel?

unPAved Pennsylvania stepped in to help Barn Gravel grow by providing permits, insurance, branding, and a formal structure. While this support helped the event expand, it also unintentionally softened some of the grassroots, social spirit that defined Barn Gravel.

So, we are handing the event back to local leadership, led by Aaron Johnson of GO GRAVA, in hopes that this beloved group ride—which has happened annually for six years—can continue in the spirit in which it began.

Gravel, farm roads, dirt paths, and singletrack… You can ride all that in 1 day right here in Berks county!

Supports Helping Harvest, and we will ask every participant to bring a food item or cash donation during registration to support local hunger efforts and farmers.

1st Trailhead at Holmesville, NE with restrooms and drinking fountains is approx 7.5 miles from the start (round trip mileage is 15 miles). We will have SAG supplies available.

2nd Trailhead at Blue Springs, NE with restrooms and drinking water is approx. 12.5 miles from the start (round trip mileage is 25 miles). We will have SAG supplies available.

EventName: Corsa Coppi Criterium -- Event #8 in the 2026 MABRA Road Series
EventNotes:
WELCOME!   Squadra Coppi is excited to welcome racers, families, friends, and spectators to the inaugural Corsa Coppi Criterium at Chinquapin Park in Alexandria, VA. Located in the heart of Alexandria, the event features a fast and technical loop course, closed to vehicle traffic, that is suitable for riders of all categories. We look forward to hosting a competitive and enjoyable day of racing while showcasing one of Alexandria's premier recreational destinations.

THE COURSE:  The race will be contested on a 0.5-mile closed-loop course utilizing Chinquapin Dr. around Chinquapin Park. The course features smooth pavement, multiple turns, and excellent spectator viewing opportunities. Riders should familiarize themselves with the course prior to racing and are encouraged to participate in any scheduled course preview sessions.

COURSE ADDRESS:

Chinquapin Park
3210 King Street
Alexandria, VA 22302

DIRECTIONS:  Chinquapin Park is conveniently located in Alexandria, Virginia, just minutes from Interstate 395, Duke Street, and Old Town Alexandria. Participants are encouraged to use Google Maps navigation to the event address listed above.

PARKING:  Parking will be available at the First Baptist Church of Alexandria:

First Baptist Church of Alexandria
2932 King Street
Alexandria, VA 22302

Please respect all parking instructions, posted signage, and volunteer direction. Our ability to continue using these facilities depends on participants parking only in approved areas and leaving the facilities clean and undamaged.

LICENSING: USAC Road rules apply.  A racing license is required to enter; please provide your USAC license # when registering online, and be prepared to show your license at check-in.  Unlicensed riders may race only in categories that are open to Novice (Cat. 5) riders, and will be charged an additional $15 in their BikeReg shopping cart for a 1-Day license.

ENTRY FEES:  The entry fee for Juniors (Racing Age 9-18) is $20.00 for all races they are eligible to enter.  The entry fee for all other riders is $50.00 for the first race and $25.00 for additional races.  Note that the multi-entry discount is applied automatically only when the entries are purchased in the same BikeReg shopping cart; otherwise use the 'Contact Us' link below to request a partial refund for the second race.  For second entries purchased on race day, inquire at the day-of registration table for a coupon code to receive the discount at checkout.  BikeReg assesses a service charge for each entry purchased.  A surcharge of $10.00 will be assessed for adult riders purchasing their first entry on race day; for Junior riders the surcharge will be $5.00.  Entry fees are non-refundable.

RACE DAY REGISTRATION & CHECK-IN:  Race-day registration and rider check-in will be located near the start/finish area. Riders must check in and collect their race numbers prior to competing. Check-in will open at least 1 hour prior to the start of the first scheduled race and will close 20 minutes prior to the scheduled start time of each race.

Please arrive early to allow sufficient time for parking, check-in, number pickup, and course familiarization.

Entry fees will be collected only through BikeReg.  There will be no in-person sales at the event.  Riders who pre-register by the Thursday 8:30 AM closing of pre-registration will have pre-assigned bibs, and will receive email notification of their bib numbers prior to race day; riders who register after the page re-opens will be assigned bibs at the event.  If you are pre-registered, please memorize your bib number; if you have a USA Cycling Annual license, please pull the license up on your phone before you get in line to check in.  

PRO TIP #1:  don't wait until you go to register (or worse, until race day) to renew your USAC racing license, as it can take a couple of days for the renewal to propagate through the USAC system before BikeReg (and we!) can see it.

PRO TIP #2:  hands-down, the best way to always have your USAC racing license on-hand is to add it to your Google or Apple wallet.  Login to your USAC account to get started.

If you miss the closing of pre-registration, you must complete the registration process on BikeReg when the page re-opens, then wait to receive your confirmation email before getting in line to check in at the event.  Present your confirmation, along with your USA Cycling racing license (or if you are racing on a 1-Day license, your BikeReg receipt), and we will issue your bib.  Registration will be open for each category until 20 minutes prior to the scheduled start of the race.  Don't be “that guy/gal” – plan ahead and arrive timely!

START TIMES:  All race start times are estimates and may be adjusted based on race-day conditions, field sizes, or unforeseen circumstances. Participants should listen for announcements and remain near the staging area prior to their scheduled events.

WEATHER:  The event will be held rain or shine. Race officials reserve the right to modify, shorten, delay, or cancel races if conditions are determined to be unsafe.

COMBINED CATEGORY RACES will race together as one field, and will be uploaded to USA Cycling and road-results as a single field, but will be scored separately for podiums and prize lists.  The Junior fields will start separately by 2 age groups, and will be scored separately.  The Masters 45+ field will start 1 minute ahead of the Masters 55+/65+ field, and each age group will be scored separately for podiums and prize lists.

SPECTATORS:  Spectators are encouraged to attend and enjoy the racing from designated viewing areas around the course. Please remain clear of the race roadway and follow all instructions from race officials and volunteers.

COMMUNITY PARTNERS:  We would like to thank Alexandria City High School, First Baptist Church of Alexandria, the City of Alexandria, our volunteers, sponsors and local cycling community for helping make this event possible.

QUESTIONS:  for registration or eligibility inquiries, contact SpacemanEventServices@gmail.com; for general race inquiries, contact squadracoppibod@googlegroups.com.

EventName: The Ride Series MTB Skills Clinics: JUMP BASICS Sat 8-11 & JUMP PROGRESSION Sun 8-11
EventNotes:
The Ride Series is different. Your expectations should be high as you enter the hospitality of our classroom setting. A comfortable Kijaro chair awaits your presence and the cover our 10x20 tents provides reprieve from the elements. Prepare yourself to be immersed in an environment that provides the perfect opportunity for you to be open to embracing and practicing the proper technique. Instant feedback from our coaching staff will have you progressing like never before! Are YOU ready??

JUMP ESSENTIALS: 

We get it, everyone wants to jump! However, most people don't embrace the technique AND psychology behind doing it well. You have to understand the what and why before you can start to build confidence with the how, that's what this session is for. Not only will you build a solid understanding of what NEEDS to happen, you'll also get plenty of reps working through the steps of how it needs to happen, all in a safe and controlled environment. 

Topics Covered: 

Riders will get plenty of reps on multiple takeoffs/landings and Rich will work through multiple rounds of video so you can see exactly what's working and what isn't. 

JUMP PROGRESSION Session: Ground School and All American Hero's Jumpline

This event is all about getting comfortable in the air. That starts with a solid understanding of what it takes to get into the air properly. It's also critical to get as MANY reps as possible in a controlled environment and that's what the TRS ground school setting gives you.

Rich will break down the dynamics involved with jumping a bike. Based on over 40 years of experience, he will guide you through his real world experience and provide key insight and cues on what to do. 

After showcasing the proper technique, you'll work through a series of reps and the distance will incrementally increase as your comfort level increases. Analysis and feedback using slow motion video will have you "busting big" in no time.

There's no substitute for experience when it comes to jumping a bike. The only problem is that experience in the right setting can be hard to come by. You'll get tons reps on our jump lines and receive valuable feedback in the moment.
RIDERS MUST HAVE:
- Experience jumping
- Full suspension bikes with suspension in working order
- Full safety gear including pads (Full Face helmet not required, but suggested)

This class is intended for riders with jump experience and will move at a specified pace. Coaching staff reserves the right to hold riders to pre determined distances based on performance.

Please reach out if you are unsure if this class is a proper fit for you.

Cranky Monkey Mountain Bike Race

The Cranky Monkey heads to Rosaryville State Park in 2026!  Join us for an awesome day of bike racing and community.

Race Date: Sunday August 30, 2026 (rain date 9/27)

Volunteer sign-up

Race Courses: 4 XC courses varying in length from about 6 miles miles to over 30 miles.  See course notes below for course information and maps.

  • Beginner – 5.6ish miles
  • Base –  9ish miles
  • Sport – 20ish miles
  • Expert – 30ish miles

Rosaryville State Park in Upper Marlboro, MD is an absolute gem and one of the most beginner friendly and fun parks in our area for mountain biking. We’ve been hosting races at Rosaryville for over 15 years and are excited to bring back the Cranky Monkey to this very special park. We’ve designed four courses for this race – beginner, base, sport, and expert. They are each described below. All courses start and end at the day use pavilions near the power lines that traverse the park. The start of the race is designed to allow for an exciting, but not overly crowded race start.

  • Beginner (~5.6 miles) – the beginner course is just shy of 6 miles long with about 400 feet of elevation change. It is designed to provide a safe and achievable entrance to mountain bike racing for participants of a variety of ages. The course highlights the western portion of the Perimeter Trail, which is the main multi-use trail in the park.
  • Base (~9 miles) – the base course is a step up fro the beginner course both in length and difficulty. It is about 9 miles in length with 600 feet of elevation change. The base course also highlights the western portion of the Perimeter Trail and also adds in the more technical Tilly Trail.
  • Sport (~20 miles) – the sport course provides a grand tour of the Rosaryville trail system and comes in at about 20 miles in length with about 1,500 feet of elevation change. The sport course highlights the entire Perimeter and Tilly Trails plus a bit.
  • Expert (~30 miles) – the expert course provides a grand route of the Rosaryville trail system and comes in about about 30 miles in length with about 2,200 feet of elevation change. The expert course highlights two complete loops of the Perimeter and Tilly Trails plus a bit.

All the trails at Rosaryville are largely maintained by volunteers organized by the Mid-Atlantic Off-Road Enthusiasts (MORE).  All racers will have the opportunity to donate to the Rosaryville Trail Fund during registration.

Race Day Schedule
Sunday August 30, 2026 (rain date 9/27)

  • 8:00am – Beginner race start
  • 9:00am – Base race start
  • 10:00am – Sport and Expert races start

Race Start Procedures
We are separating each race into wave starts to allow enough space to spread out the field of riders.  Each wave will be separated by a few minutes. Exact start times will be based on the number of riders in each class.

EventName: Bike Hub Sunday Epic V5 - Grass Mtn Sufferfest
EventNotes:
The Bike Hub is proud to announce our Sunday Epic ride series! These are all-day rides featuring some of the best mixed-terrain riding the tri-state area has to offer. Forgotten woods roads, fast gravel, rugged singletrack, and even a bit of hike-a-bike. These rides will be long, difficult, and absolutely beautiful. While there is no perfect bike for a Sunday Epic, anything with around a 2 inch tire will work. More details on terrain will be included in each event post. Sunday Epic's will be held the third Sunday of every month from April-September. Start location may vary, but will usually end will some sort of food and drink situation. Wheels down at 8am always.

 This one is gonna be extra tough. Bring a mountain bike of some sort, curly bars may not get you far. My goal here was to put together a ride with the toughest possible terrain and most amount of climbing in the least mileage. Enter the Grass Mtn Sufferset. If you've never visited this area you are in for a treat. Starts and ends at the Shaftsbury Historical Society on 7A, park by the red barn.

 

A few notes on the nitty-gritty of these rides. 

  • Sunday Epic's are fully self supported. Bring everything you need to successfully finish the route. We expect you to carry basics like spare tube, pump, multi-tool, patch kit, food and water, etc. Although we occasionally stop at a convenience store, there are many times where the ride is too remote for that to be an option.
  • We generally try to ride together, but you are welcome to do your own thing as long as you have the route. Group pace usually hovers somewhere around the 10mph average mark, but may be slower depending on terrain/climbing.
  • Expect this to take a good chunk of the day. Occasional stops for snacks etc. We move pretty continuously, but also aren't in a rush. 

RideWithGPS link here.

Note that we don't charge anything for these rides, but we do welcome donations! We are a community-based 501c3 nonprofit focused on removing barriers to cycling for all within the tri-state area. We provide education, free access to bikes and cycling accessories, and provide a place for people of all ages and abilities to connect through cycling. Please read this!
 

Welcome to our FREE monthly ride! Ride start times vary by season to give us the best trail conditions and safest experience—May through September we roll out at 9:00 AM CT, and October through April we begin at 2:00 PM CT. We meet at the lower parking lot at Turkey Mountain Urban Wilderness Park, 6800 S Elwood Ave, Tulsa, OK 74132. Restrooms are available.

 

We will have ride leaders for skill levels between Beginner to Advanced. If you're new to mountain biking, OR have never taken WeROK’s Fundamentals, or other formal fundamentals skills clinics (even if you have been riding some), we REQUIRE YOU to start with the WeROK Fundamental Skills Session during registration. Regardless of your riding experience we feel taking this skills session will help improve your riding and create a better riding experience for all.

 

Loaner Bikes: Please refer to your registration confirmation letter. 
 

Cancellation/Bad Weather Policy: If bad weather develops we aim to cancel the event by 7:00 am the day of the ride.  Stay tuned to social media for announcements. We also follow Trailbot, in case Turkey Mountain trails are “closed” or “delayed”.  We do not have “rain dates”. 

 

Choosing appropriate group: First choose your riding and fitness level, then choose the best description among the groups. Once a group fills, the waitlist option will open. If you have a friend with the same skill level with whom you want to ride, help us out by registering together ASAP, in the same ride level, AND in same group number. Other than cancellations, we CANNOT GUARANTEE we can make any changes to groups, especially at the last minute, since we have group size restrictions. This delivers the best possible ride experience for all! If you don't end up riding with your friends, don't worry, you'll have the opportunity to make new ones!
 

Not sure which group to join? Ride levels are based on YOUR CURRENT skill and endurance levels. We want everyone to have the best and safest experience possible so we use a “rating” system to help align you with the right ride group. Please review the skills, endurance, mileage and proposed trails. Being in the right group makes a better, safer ride for all. If you are still unsure about which group might be for you just contact us at ride@werok.org. P.S. It is perfectly fine to “repeat” a level! Mastery of ALL levels takes time and practice. Please don’t rush yourself, nor succumb to peer pressure. NOTE: WeROK’s skill level names and colors are relative to Turkey Mountain trails. Other trail systems’ color designations could mean their Blue is (y)our Black, so be wise!
 

Advancing to next groups: A great way to know if you are ready to progress to the next ride level is if (1) you felt comfortable with skills necessary at your current level, and (2) you were able to keep up with the ride leader the entire ride and felt like you could have ridden longer. 

 

GROUP CHOICES:
 

1. FUNDAMENTAL SKILLS SESSION 

Select this group if you have never ridden a mountain bike, it’s been longer than you’d like to admit, OR you've never taken any type of basic mtb skills lessons before. Welcome! You have to start somewhere and this is the place! Even the most advanced riders should brush up on these essentials, and certainly, if you feel rusty, this session will help you. This session will cover the fundamentals of mountain biking, and then you'll hit the trail for a 2-3 mile ride. Successful completion of WeROK’s Fundamentals (or its equivalent) is required for advancement to next groups. Departure from this policy requires approval by a WeROK ride leader.

  • Skill Level: Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals are required (we may have loaner pedals available; email us ahead of time at ride@werok.org).
  • Skills you can perform: no requirement, you will definitely learn a skill or two after this session. 
  • Fitness Level: No requirement other than participate in possible heat for up to 2 hours.
  • Example of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, no rocks; double track near Bomb Cellar; the grassy fields; the Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop. 

2. FUNDAMENTALS TO GREEN Group

Select this group if you have taken the Fundamental Skills session, you feel more confident with those skills, and you are looking for a very easy-going transition to green trails. You will have a skills refresher for up to 15 minutes.

  • Skill Level: Confident Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals strongly encouraged (see above re: loaner pedals).
  • Skills you can perform: Staying upright while pedaling, skills learned in Fundamentals Group are beginning to make sense, and your confidence is growing.
  • Fitness Level: Completed a Fundamentals session with minimal fatigue
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with occasional flat, mellow rocks or roots, no significant downhill or uphill; Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop; the very first section of LoChi Connector.
  • Duration: 3-5 miles, maybe longer in cooler weather, no longer than 1.5 hours after refresher portion

3. GREEN Group
You’ve ridden on the dirt trails multiple times by now, and you’re getting the hang of things. You’re mastering the Fundamentals Skills, and your bike operating and handling skills feel smoother. No Fundamentals refresher portion provided.

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: Level pedals while coasting; one finger braking; becoming more comfortable with neutral and ready positions; and smoother corners/berms.
  • Fitness level: Able to ride steady at a comfortable pace for 30 minutes on easy terrain, and may need a breather while climbing, or at the top.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with a variety of low, smooth surface changes; more variety of up and downhill; LoChi; UHF or All Up with rests.
  • Duration: 5-7 miles,1.5 to 2.0 hours 

4. OPEN Group

Looking for new challenges! You are ready to explore more trail features (obstacles) and a variety of up and downhills, with limited stops. Mileage varies. No Fundamentals refresher provided. 

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus-to-Intermediate.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: GREEN skills are solid, but you’re out of saddle more instinctively with level pedals; in and out of neutral/ready position more smoothly; frequent appropriate shifting; smoother, smoother berms and corners; want to ride across straight bridges and skinnies 3-5 feet wide; comfortable choosing lines through rockier terrain, or between tight trees.
  • Fitness level: You’re riding a few times a week. Can ride a WeROK course continuously unless learning steep or more technical terrain. Pushing the pace uphill.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, more roots and rocks, twists and turns. The small bridge on OLD Lo Chi, All Up, UHF, Stay Gold Loop, Naharkey clockwise, maybe counterclockwise. Sessioning features within your skill set, such as the small skinny on Family Loop.
  • Duration: 8-10 miles, 2 hours with some stopping.

EventNotes:
Stop number one of the River Valley Cross Series p/b Shimano!

8/30- Blunt Park CX - Springfield, MA

9/5- Hydra CX - Holyoke, MA

9/26- Kilowatt Cross - Northfield, MA

10/18 Treehouse CX - South Deerfield, MA

11/7- West hill CX- Putney VT

 

To promote our local juniors, ALL Juniors get to race for free at Blunt park!

The course will be basically the same great course as in past years with a few modifications.  It is approximate 2+ miles long and is made up of pavement, grassy fields, and single/double track.  It’s flat, fast and has more than it's fair share of turns.  Bring the family as venue is very spectator friendly with a fun atmosphere for the spectators. Also, please be prepared as the park has a nominal parking fee for all vehicles.  

PLEASE PRE-REGISTER! 2nd race only $10.  Field limits 20 min, 75 max for all categories.  

We are offering a Cat 5/Novice field for Men and Women. This field is intended for new riders and racers looking to try out the sport.

DIRECTIONS:

Blunt Park is just minutes from major highways (MA Pike, RT 91 & RT 291).

From East or West: Mass Pike (Rte. I-90) to exit 6 (Route 291).  Take 291 West to Exit 5 (Rt 20 West).  At first lights take a left onto Roosevelt Ave.  Park is about a mile up on the right.
From North or South: Take Rt 91 North or South (depending on direction) to RT 291 East.  Follow 291 East to Exit 5B (Rt 20). At first lights take a left onto Roosevelt Ave.  Park is about a mile up on the right.

EventName: RCV Prospective Member Practice and Tryouts
EventNotes:
Interested riders and families are invited to attend our Prospective Rider practice and tryout at North Chevy Chase Local Park (4105 Jones Bridge Road, Chevy Chase). Junior riders must be 9 years old by December 31, 2027 (CX racing age is determined as of the end of the following calendar year). 

Riders should bring a bike (mountain or cyclocross), helmet, and water if they plan to participate in practice/ tryout for RCV. Any racks, bags, bottle cages, etc. should be removed from bikes. Children will be lifting bikes over barriers and extra weight makes this very challenging.

Riders invited to join the team will have the opportunity to rent a cyclocross bike from the RCV loaner bike fleet. Before and after practices, coaches will meet with riders and families to learn more about the rider, their interest in cycle, and availability for practices and races. Riders and families are encouraged to attend the entire practice to observe the drills and workouts of a typical practice, as well as meet current families and riders. 


Practice may be cancelled in the event of inclement weather. 
 
To learn more about Rock Creek Velo, visit https://rockcreekvelo.org/.   

Questions? Contact Ashlea Gray at  membership@rockcreekvelo.org.

EventName: DRRT Technical Trails Workshop - Port Jervis
EventNotes:
DRRT Technical Trails Workshop - Port Jervis

Let's get technical.  This enduro style workshop will focus on the technical terrain found at Port Jervis. We'll tackle small trail jumps and drops as we work on line choice and technical riding.

When: August 30
Time: 10 am - 1 pm
Who:  Riders looking to improve their technical riding skills
Cost:  $175
Where:  Port Jervis Watershed Trails Port Jervis NY

This session is limited to 6 participants - prior mountain bike experience required.

A mountain bike in good working condition is required.  Helmet required.  Flat pedals, elbow and knee pads recommended. This workshop take place rain or shine.

---------

About DRRT:

Dirt Rock n Root Training's owner Kathi Krause has been around the bike block – from velodrome and road racing to cyclocross, XC and finally her true love: downhill. She spent a decade on the Pro downhill circuit, stacking up three Masters World DH Championships, five national titles and a win at the legendary Kamikaze Downhill.

After 25 years of racing, Kathi shifted gears to coaching and founded Dirt Rock n Root Training in 2011 . Since then, she's been helping riders find their flow on everything from lift-accessed bike parks to rocky, rooty singletrack. You'll find her leading her Technical Trail series of clinics in North Jersey or running women's clinics at Mountain Creek Bike Park.  Her mission? Simple:  Get more women and kids on bikes, help them crush fear and build a community that rides hard and supports harder.

When not coaching, you can find Kathi out doing what she loves most - shredding the rocks and roots of NJ or dropping into her home trails at Mountain Creek Bike Park.
PresentedBy: Dirt Rock n Root Training LLC

Categories.CategoryName: Women's Cyclocross Skills Clinic - Full Event

EventNotes:
Women's Cyclocross Skills Clinic — Northeast Ohio Cyclocross

Sunday, August 30th | 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM 

Location: Cumberland Park, 1740 Cumberland Rd, Cleveland Hts, OH 44118

Whether you're brand new to 'cross or looking to sharpen your handling before race day, this clinic is your chance to build confidence on the bike in a fun, low-pressure setting. All levels are welcome — this is the most accessible discipline in cycling, and there's no better way to try it out or level up your skills.

We're building a mini-course covering every core cyclocross skill: mounts and dismounts, barriers, cornering, carries, cambers, and starts. You'll work through each skill station with course breakdown, bike handling tips, and hands-on coach feedback along the way.

This clinic will be held rain or shine — both are part of racing 'cross, so come dressed for the weather and ready to ride. We do have a pavilion to take breaks and keep gear dry!

Parking: Pool parking area next to the basketball courts. Our pavilion is behind the pool area. 

Cost: Free 

Bikes: Any bike works — cyclocross, gravel, or mountain bike in good repair are all welcome. We will have Jerry Shere available to help with any mechanical issues that arise during the clinic

RSVP: [www.bikereg.com/neocx-clinic  contact korinevanscoach@gmail.com or toveshere@gmail.com  ] 

Your Coaches

Tove Shere

Tove holds a BA in Physical Education and has worked as a personal trainer, strength and conditioning coach, and USA Triathlon coach since 1995. A 7x National Champion in Cyclocross as a Masters athlete, she also earned a silver medal at the 2008 Cyclocross Masters World Championships in Belgium. Beyond 'cross, Tove has competed across a wide range of disciplines — time trials, duathlon, triathlon, snowshoe, and cross country skiing — bringing decades of multi-sport experience to her coaching. 

 

 

Korin Evans 

Korin is the founder of Whole Body Athlete, a strength and nutrition coaching business for active women and endurance athletes. She's a certified personal trainer, nutrition coach and menopause coaching specialist who has worked in health and fitness since 2019. She's competed in many cycling disciplines including; road racing, criteriums, mountain bike and gravel, but cyclocross is her most favorite. She was the Ohio State Masters Champion in Cyclocross in 2022, finisher at Crushar in the Tushar Gravel, Beaver, Utah in 2019 and has been racing competitively for 13 years.

Schedule

10:00 AM – 2:00 PM: Skills Clinic 

Rotating stations covering mounts/dismounts, barriers, cornering, carries, cambers, and starts, with coach instruction and feedback throughout. 

We’ll start with a course walk, move through each station, learn ‘course breakdown’ then run practice laps at the end.

What to Bring

  • Any off-road bike in good working condition (cyclocross, gravel or mountain bike)

  • Helmet is REQUIRED
  • Water Bottle
  • Snacks, water and electrolytes will be provided by Whole Body Athlete Coaching

  • Weather-appropriate clothing — this clinic runs rain or shine — we have a pavilion to keep gear dry in wet weather!

It's a race against the clock! The Calaveras Time Trial by Team Fremont is a great race for everyone of all different skill levels on the beautiful Calaveras Road in Sunol, CA. Whether you are a seasoned road racer, triathlete, a junior racer or a beginner, we have a category for you.

REGISTRATION: Online Registration ONLY. Closes midnight, Thursday August 27. 2026. Entry are fees $50 except Juniors Cat $20, fees include $3 NCNCA and $5.99 USAC insurance surcharges. The Calaveras TT is part of the NCNCA BAR/BAT, NCNCA Juniors Series & the 2025 NCNCA Junior District TT Championship.

DIRECTIONS: From I-680, take the Highway 84 exit and go north on Paloma Road (84) to Sunol. Bear left on 84 onto Niles Canyon road and then turn right on to Main Street to Sunol Glen School. Follow signs to parking. From Niles Canyon (Fremont), exit at Sunol turn right on Main Street. Follow signs to parking.

COURSE: 10 miles on excellent to fair pavement, this is an out and back course. One major climb of 350 feet going to the turn. Start and finish are located approx. 300 yards South of I-680 on Calaveras Road. Turn at the 5.0 miles mark, 1 mile up the hill and past Geary road and retrace. Juniors 9-10 will have a 5 mile course.

WARM UP: Trainer or rollers. No warming up on course.

RULES: USAC Permit 202X-XXXX. A 2026 USAC license required, or purchase a 1-day license during pre-registration or on Bike Reg. No time trial bikes are allowed for all Junior Categories, see USAC Rule 1I5 pg. 31. All USA Cycling rules and code of conduct will be enforced. Juniors 15-18 up may use Time Trial Bikes in non-junior categories. MERCKX: no aero bars or clip-ons, no TT helmet (or face shield), and no wheels deeper than 60mm (paying homage to how Merckx set the hour record in 1972). All other categories may use Time Trial Bikes (except U14).

Start times will be posted at OnTheDay.net 

We'll email you a link to the start lists on August 28th. First rider will depart the start at 8:01 and following riders will depart in the above category order at 60 second intervals. Field limited to 360 total start slots due to parking constraints.

SECOND RIDES: There will be a break after the Junior categories to enable as many 2nd rides as possible. Race Merckx or Masters before the break and your category after the break.

2026 NCNCA Junior District Championship is as follows: The riders must hold an annual license: riders from outside the NCNCA District are welcomed to compete, the title/jersey will be awarded to an annual license holder residing in the NCNCA Region. Juniors in the 9-10 year old category is part of the non-championship category and will ride a 5 mile course.

USAC 7J3 Eligiblity: (a) to be eligible for a State Championship jersey or medal, a rider must hold a current USA Cycling annual license and reside in the state as shown as the rider’s license. (b) State championships are open to US Citizens and permanent residents (green card) with a USA Cycling annual license. (c) Members of UCI Road teams are not eligible for road championships unless there is a separate class for them. (d) at the option of the Administrators, State Championships may include rider who are ineligible for the championship but championships will be awarded to only riders who are eligible.

EventName: Northeast Velodrome Try the Track Clinic - 08/31/2026
EventNotes:
Try the Track Clinic – Northeast Velodrome

This clinic is for riders new to fixed gear and velodrome riding. It provides the skills and knowledge needed to begin riding and racing at the Northeast Velodrome.

Skills Covered

Riding a Fixed Gear

  • Starting and stopping without brakes
  • Controlling speed through pedaling
  • Riding smoothly and predictably

Track Awareness & Etiquette

  • Understanding track layout and lane terminology
  • Riding the banking and holding a line
  • Group riding fundamentals and communication

Paceline & Racing Skills

  • Riding close to others in a controlled setting
  • Paceline basics: rotating, pulling, and rejoining
  • Introduction to track race concepts and rules

Additional Information

Track bike rental is included. If renting, bring your own pedals and cycling shoes. Helmet required.

If possible, provide your frame size and saddle height (measured from center of bottom bracket to top of saddle) in advance to assist with bike setup.

Price: $30
Field limit: 8 riders

Successful completion of this clinic certifies you to participate in other Northeast Velodrome sessions and events.

EventNotes:
Day of Registration will be available. Adults are $40 & Juniors are $25.

Day of registration spots are limited to the remaining spaces in each field. We cannot guarantee that you will be able to race.

We are proud to present the Rocky Hill CX Series as a centralized location for our youth teams to practice at (5:00 PM), and a fun, no-pressure, training race for those looking to enjoy cyclocross racing (5:35 PM for the Juniors and 6:15 PM Open Race). Thanks to the Town of Rocky Hill Parks and Rec and our partner clubs for allowing this to happen!

Volunteers are needed to make this event successful. Sign up to volunteer and you will receive reimbursement on your entry fee. CLICK HERE TO HELP OUT

Series Dates:
This 4-week training series will take place on 4 Wednesdays in August/September. August 26th, Sept 2nd, Sept 9th, and Sept 16th. With respect to the Town of Rocky Hill and their beautiful park, we will cancel due to rain and wet conditions that will be especially damaging to the venue. In this case, we will provide a credit to all participants and you will be notified of a cancelation via email!

A fun, safe and positive weekly Junior Practice Session
This practice is hosted by CCAP staff and regional team coaches. Licensed junior riders under 18 and middle/high schoolers can enjoy a no-pressure practice session at 5:00 PM. Any junior that wants to ride must be at least 9 years old (cyclocross racing age = age on Dec 31st of the 2026 year) and are welcome to race in the Junior Race. All training activities and races will be started with instruction from CCAP coaches and staff. All youth riders, 18 and under, are welcome to participate in the practice for $10. Riders that are on CCAP registered teams may participate in the practice at no charge.

Fun, safe and competitive racing for all
Fun, friendly, and competitive racing for everyone from novice racers to experienced Category 1 Racers. The wide variety of skill levels makes for an informal, no-pressure vibe. 

All riders must have a USA Cycling License. If you don't have one, one-day beginner licenses may be purchased for $15 and are valid for a single day. One-day beginner licenses may only be purchased by new riders or Category 5 riders.

Equipment
All USAC Rules apply. All riders must wear a helmet. A cyclocross bike or mountain bike (without bar-ends) is suggested. No BMX bikes allowed.

New to cyclocross?
Check out THIS VIDEO to learn what it's all about!

For full information about our weekly race series, we encourage you to visit our website: https://catamountoutdoor.org/race-series-weekly/

 

In the event that the race is cancelled for inclement weather, your entry can be transferred to a different week.

 

A huge thank you to our 2026 series sponsors! 

Gold Level

Central Vermont Runners, MoveWell, SDR Clothing Company

The CXTT is a series of practice races. Cyclists race against the clock on a 2-3 mile course in Kingswood Park in Deerfield Township. This gives the everyone an opportunity to reconnect with the cyclocross community, tune their equipment and training, and give folks new to the sport to try it out in a no-pressure environment.

The CXTT will be on Wednesdays, August 12, 19, 26, and September 2. Riders are called to line up around 6:15, with the first rider starting at 6:30.

Single week registration is $15/rider. Registration and signed waiver is due on noon on race day. You will receive a race number which you will need for the whole series

World famous Wednesday Worlds cyclocross practice at Holster Park, in Clifton NJ. Come build skills and fitness for the cyclocross racing season. 

Wheels down 5:30 - we will do a mix of skills and drills to build fitness before moving on to hot lap and race pace efforts. Session ends around 730 depending on weather, daylight and conditions.  Meet at the tennis courts.  

Location:  https://www.google.com/maps/place/Holster+Park/@40.8593319,-74.188589,16z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x89c2ffb3b0eb8ab1:0xa15abc2860c1a7ec!8m2!3d40.8593319!4d-74.1860141!16s%2Fg%2F1tdwr0j4?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI0MDgyOC4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D

Important info:

  • This is a training group, not a race. Beginners are encouraged and very welcome, but be please be aware that cyclocross is physically demanding and requires a fair level of fitness.   
  • We ride in a public park and conditions may change each week. We are guests in the park and will do everything to keep it clean and respect the rules.
  • We respect others in the park. We respect each other. No fighting. All are welcome.  
  • Helmet is required. Bring a cyclocross (or MTB) bike in good working order.
  • Park on the road between the school and the baseball field. Do NOT park in the fenced area behind the school.  
  • Event may be cancelled due to weather.  Check your email and join the Facebook Group for the latest info.
  • Be nice to each other.

*racing start at 5:30 PM sharp due to limited daylight!

  • 6:00 PM – Intermediate/B Races (30 mins)

Spring Hill Parking: Use the commuter lot—**please avoid parking under the trees on Barbour (porta-john side)**.  #crossiscoming

Four Crit Races - Three Nights

City of Tulsa Safety Center: 10926 E Cameron St, Tulsa, OK 74116

Numbers: All riders are responsible for keeping their number for both races. If racers need a new number there will be a $10 charge. 

Day of Reg: $50 for first race $10 for second

Welcome to the first annual Interlude 360 mile ultra bike race! 

22+ miles of single track - 92 miles of pavement - 246+ miles of gravel and B roads

Start Location - Red Wheel Bike shop - 400 West Main Street Jefferson City, Missouri 65101

Starting time - 0900 - Friday - September 4th 2026  (Registration Sign in will begin at 08:00 am)

Rules

Every year the rules can change. The fastest participant is usually the one that knows the rules.

This is not a closed course you are responsible for your person and all belongings you take or acquire along the way. You will have to carry your bike at some time. You could definitely get your feet wet. everyone and any one that may be affiliated with Red wheel Bike shop and Interlude bike race is not held liable for any of your actions before, during, or after this event.

Drafting is allowed

No littering

Every Participant must utilize a front and rear light at night.

If you go off course you must reenter at the same place. 

You can secure a sleeping arrangement before the begins.

Everyone is allowed to have support during the event. This means food, water and even utilizing a vehicle to sleep in. Hopefully this will allow beginner and new ultra cyclists to  test their abilities before jumping into a even bigger event.

Don't be a dick!

Allowed - 

  • Aero bars
  • Super Tuck
  • Super Aero helmets
  • Any width of handlebars
  • Drop bar mountain bikes
  • Any sock height

Race route - The route will start at Jefferson City and move north to Macon, Missouri and circle back.

This is the unofficial route.

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/55489174

*August 1st the race route will be posted on the internet and e-mailed to all participants. 

Popular Questions: 

Will there be aid stations? No you will need to bring or purchase every thing you need to survive.

What type of bike will I need? That is up to you! As race director, I believe a gravel bike with a minimum of 45mm tires will be needed. I would not recommend a road bike. Any mountain bike would work.

Is there a cut off time to finish?  No  - If you take longer than 72 hours you will be considered a finisher but no one will be at the finish line to meet you. 

Will there be SAG if I can't finish? Yes, If you need help getting back to the finish line for any uncertain reason a SAG driver will be of assistance. Please understand you could be waiting a while if you are at the other end of the course. Once you decide you can not finish the course you are considered DNF. You are able to have help from any friends, team or family. 

Where can I sleep on the course? Sleeping is always an option. Motels, AIRBB, VRBO, AND campsites are preferred. If you decide to sleep any where else know the law. Don't Trespass. Stay out of ditches. Be aware of your surroundings. You are welcome to sleep in a sag drivers vehicle. 

Can I ride without a Spot Tracker? No, The Spot Tracker is not only for friends and family to follow you but also for safety.

RACE RULES!!!! WE ARE NOW A PART OF THE CHAINBUSTER'S ENDURANCE SERIES!!! FOR SPECIFIC RULES CHECK OUT CHAINBUSTER'S RULES

All participants will be required to wear a bicycle helmet at all times while riding. Penalty is DQ.

Outside (non racer) assistance is only permitted in the pit area. Non racers may not assist out on the course. Racers may assist other racers and are encouraged to do so.

All food and drink for the race must be either carried with the racer or staged in the pit area. There will be 1 water stop on the course as well.

Due to the number of racers on the trail, earbuds are prohibited.

Race numbers must be visible at all times and must be mounted to the handlebars on the front of the bike.

Littering is not permitted. First offense is 15 minute penalty, 2nd offense is DQ.

Cutting the course is not permitted. Penalty is DQ and public ridicule.

In the event of an unfixable mechanical, the racer must complete the lap along the entire course with his/her bike to receive credit for the lap. You MAY back track or shortcut back to the pit to fix your bike, but you will not receive credit for that lap. Do not enter the timing/exchange area if you are coming back from an incomplete lap. Please be honest.

Please exercise caution and good sportsmanship when passing other racers on the trail. Announce your intention to pass rather than just forcing your way by with no warning. Most riders will gladly let you pass.

Solos need to complete one lap to be considered official finishers. Teams need each person to complete at least one lap to be considered official finishers.

Once you reach your pit, you may change any equipment you want, including bikes, and you may stay there as long as you'd like.

WINNERS WILL BE DETERMINED BY NUMBER OF LAPS COMPLETED IN THE GIVEN TIME. IF MULTIPLE RIDERS HAVE THE SAME NUMBER OF LAPS THEN LAP TIMES WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE WINNER!

Down for Gravel

Date: Saturday, September 5, 2026

Location: 101 Applegate Lane, West Newfield, Maine


 

Event Overview:

Down for Gravel is a gravel cycling event that brings riders together for a challenging and rewarding day on the backroads of western Maine. The start and finish are situated on the picturesque Mirror Lake, providing a scenic backdrop for the day’s ride. Routes wind through forest roads, rolling terrain, and offer stunning views—including glimpses of Mount Washington on clear days. Whether you’re looking to push your limits or enjoy a solid day of riding with great company, this event is all about community and the shared experience of gravel cycling.


 

Riders can choose from multiple route options to match their goals for the day. Each course is designed to provide a mix of smooth gravel, rugged sections, and plenty of climbing. The ride is untimed—this is about the experience, not the results.


 

Sunday Cyclocross & Camping:

The weekend kicks off on Saturday with a gravel ride, trail running race and cyclocross clinics.  Offering fast-paced action and a great opportunity to warm up or spectate before Sunday CX race. Riders are encouraged to camp on-site Friday and Saturday night to soak in the atmosphere, connect with fellow cyclists, and make the most of the weekend. The event setup includes a large open field with plenty of space for camping and parking, creating a festival-like setting leading up to race day.


 

Post-Ride Gathering:

After Down For Gravel on Saturday, stick around to share stories, enjoy wood-fired pizza, and relax with a cold beer from Frost Beer Works. A post-ride swim in Mirror Lake is highly recommended—there’s no better way to cool down after a long day on the bike.


 

Location & Accessibility:

West Newfield is conveniently located about an hour’s drive from Portland, Maine, and less than two hours from Boston, making it an easy weekend getaway for gravel riders from across the region.


 

Registration:

Sign up to secure your spot. Space is limited, and early registration is encouraged.


 

Pinebury is proud to support Down for Gravel, helping to create an event that brings people together over a shared love of gravel riding, adventure, and fun.

Inclement Weather Policy

We strive to produce a full and safe bicycle rally, but sometimes the weather conditions can impact those plans. We encourage all participants to arrive as scheduled on the morning of the ride as weather condition-related decisions will be made shortly before the ride start time of 8 AM. In many instances, weather conditions in one part of the State may not be impacting the event location, or weather conditions may improve in the hours preceding the event, both of which impact the ride start. In the event of light to moderate rain, and in the absence of any lightning, our goal is to proceed with the full event if road conditions are safe and will allow the bike ride to take place. If there is lightning in the area, the event will be placed into a weather hold and can be held for up to one hour. If the lightning has departed the area after one hour, the ride can proceed as planned. If there is still evidence of the potential for lightning in the area, the ride may either be shortened or canceled. The event has a one-hour weather hold time frame because the schedule impacts the safety of the event by such factors as increasing traffic on the routes as the day passes, and law enforcement and medical support schedules.

Due to the nature of bike rides taking place generally in the outdoors, weather conditions can play a large role in the production of the event. Because a significant amount of the funds collected during registration have already been expended by the day of the event, and because each event is uniquely scheduled for its date and location, registration refunds are not possible, and rescheduling the event is not feasible, therefore we have a no refund policy. We encourage all those who are pre-registered to pick up their packets with the t-shirt. T-shirts will not be mailed. Proceeds from registration fees and donations will continue to benefit the HALO fund. Thank you for your understanding of these policies. We appreciate your participation.

Day-of-race registration will be available for an extra $15 for all adult categories. Save money, register online before it closes. (Youth races can all be registered for day-of at no extra cost).

New to bike racing?: Hydra Cross is a great event to try out bike racing or cyclocross for the first time. There is a free intro to cyclocross racing clinic at 8:00 am on race day that is taught by local, friendly bike racers. Learn the basics to help you enjoy your race. Beginner races following shortly after -- novice men should sign up for the 9:00 am category 4 and beginner race and novice women should sign up for the 11:00 am women's category 4 and 5 race. Just a note on lingo, brand-new racers and novices start as 'category 5' racers. Since we are a USA Cycling sanctioned race, you will need a license but can purchase one when you register at http://bikereg.com/hydracross for $15. If you have any questions about the clinic or racing, please just shoot us an email at hydracrossrace@gmail.com and we'll respond with what you need. 

Course Description: A fun, fast, twisty course that is primarily flat but has some surprising uphill kickers. After a slightly uphill, wide start from the "Legion Shelf," the course heads towards Holyoke's "Muscle Beach" and the hilly southern end of the park. The course design takes full advantage of the elevation to make riders work–but then also brings rewards with a swooping downhill that cuts back and forth across the hill. We have some stinging off-camber sections that will require your skills, with the most challenging and decisive sector coming at the end of the course (see Youtube videos below for a preview). The course runs the full length of the long, linear park with ample opportunities for spectating, with continuous announcing throughout the race by the voice of NCC Hydra Cross 2025, Jake Kravitz. Mountain and river views abound.

Equipment Recommendation: File treads (if dry) and all-around tires will work well for most riders. The course is a mix of grass, dirt, and some pavement. New to cyclocross? Mountain bikes, in any shape, work fine for getting started racing. Road or touring bikes that allow for 32mm tires also work fine.

Race Atmosphere: Come for the race, stay for the atmosphere. Our beer garden and picnic area are family-friendly. There is a playground, splash pad, and popular skate park as well. Our race is known for its good vibes and community-driven feel. 

The excellent Thai Chili Street Food Hub will be serving food in the American Legion Parking lot at lunch time. As usual, expect the American Legion to be serving up coffee, breakfast items, beer and alcohol throughout the day, in addition to lunch and snack items.

Want to do a second race? Great, the second race is just $15, just register for two races at the same time when you sign up.

Lugar: Parque Pulaski, St. Koble Drive y Maple St, Holyoke, MA 01040

¿Eres nuevo en las carreras de bicicleta?: Hydra Cross es un evento excelente para probar correr en bicicleta o hacer ciclocrós por primera vez. Hay una clínica gratuita de introducción a las carrera de ciclocrós a las 8 am el día de la carrera que es impartida por corredores de bicicleta locales y amistosos. Aprende los conceptos básicos para ayudarte a disfrutar de tu carrera. Las carreras para principiantes empiezan poco tiempo después -- los hombres novatos deberían inscribirse para la carrera de principiantes categoría 5 de las 9 am, y las mujeres novatas deberían inscribirse para la carrera categoría 4 y 5 de las 10 am. Solo un comentario sobre la jerga, los corredores nuevos y los novatos comienzan como corredores ‘categoría 5’. Debido a que somos una carrera sancionada por USA Cycling, necesitarás una licencia, pero puedes comprar una por $15 cuando te inscribes en http://bikereg.com/hydracross. Si tienes alguna pregunta acerca de la clínica o las carreras, por favor envíanos un correo electrónico a hydracrossrace@gmail.com y te responderemos con la información que necesitas.

Descripción del Recorrido: Un recorrido divertido, rápido y sinuoso que es principalmente plano, pero tiene algunas subidas inesperadas. Después de un comienzo levemente cuesta arriba y amplio desde “Legion Shelf”, el recorrido se dirige hacia “Muscle Beach” en Holyoke y hacia el extremo sur montañoso del parque. El diseño del recorrido aprovecha al máximo la elevación para hacer trabajar a los corredores, pero también trae recompensas con un descenso en picada a través de la colina que acorta las idas y vueltas. Tenemos algunos punzantes sectores off-camber que requerirán de tus habilidades, siendo el sector más decisivo y desafiante el que está al final del recorrido (ver el video de Youtube indicado más abajo para una vista preliminar). El recorrido abarca la longitud completa del largo parque lineal, con amplias oportunidades para los espectadores, con relato continuo durante la carrera por la voz de Hydra Cross, Adam Syzmkowickz. Abundan las vistas a la montaña y al río.

Recomendaciones de Equipamiento: Neumáticos con banda de rodamiento lisa (para terreno seco) y multiuso funcionarán bien para la mayoría de los corredores. El recorrido es una combinación de pasto, tierra y algo de pavimento. ¿Eres nuevo en el ciclocrós? Las bicicletas de montaña, en cualquier estado, funcionan bien para empezar a correr. Las bicicletas de carretera o de turismo que permiten usar neumáticos de 32mm también funcionan bien.

Ambiente de Competición: Ven por la carrera, quédate por el ambiente. Nuestro patio cervecero y zona de picnic son aptos para familias. Hay un patio de juegos, juegos de agua y también un parque para patinetas muy popular. Nuestra carrera es conocida por sus buenas vibras y por la sensación de comunidad.

Stage 1/AirLine Cycles and friends are proud to bring you Belltown Throwdown Race 1 and Race 2 of the series, at the beautiful YMCA Camp Ingersoll.  This is the first two races hosted by Stage 1 at Ingersoll this year, but rest assured, the two races will be on different courses.

Want to help out?  Sign up to volunteer here by sending us an email.  We'll give you a t-shirt, some snacks and beverages, and unlimited high fives.

RACE DETAILS

BE SURE TO PREREGISTER -- DAY-OF REGISTRATION MAY NOT BE AVAILABLE!

We packed as much into this event as we could, and then we packed even more! Like all the AirLine and Stage 1 events, we want Belltown Throwdown to be a fun day of racing AND spectating; that means a fun course full of our trade mark "special features", sweet music, and big prizes.  We're also psyched to be part of the Project Mayhem CX series, which means consistent schedules, neutral support at every race, series prizes, and a cohesive calendar of great events.

What can you expect?  A great course that will be equal parts fun and challenging.  For example, this...

And this...

And this...

And, of course, plenty of this...

What else? How about just $20 for each additional race!

Just a couple of things to note about the event as you're planning to attend.

1.  All dogs must be kept on leash (6 feet or shorter).  No exceptions.  A loose dog is dangerous to itself and the racers.

2.  PRERIDING THE COURSE WILL BE AT THE DISCRETION OF THE OFFICIALS.  THE COURSE MAY NOT BE OPEN FOR PRERIDING BETWEEN RACES.  We tried to build time into the schedule to allow it, but there may not be time.    All prerides must begin AFTER the finish line and you must check with the officials/volunteers at the officals tent to see if it is permitted at that time.  If you are preriding, DO NOT PASS ANY ACTIVE RACERS.  If you pass an active racer, we reserve the right to DQ you from your event and you will not get a refund.  You have been warned.  

3.  Sunrise is at 6:22am.  Course will open for pre-ride at 6:30am and close at 8:10am.  If you want to pre-ride for the morning session, show up early.

4.  In the interest of serving our racers, if you cannot attend we will refund you for any reason at any time up to registration closing.  Email us.  If you wanna make up a funny story, great.

5.  Want to help out?  Sign up to volunteer here by sending us an email.  We'll give you a t-shirt, some snacks and beverages, and unlimited high fives.

6.  We are working on day-of registration.  We CANNOT guarantee it, but we will try, so it is better if you register in advance.  If we are able to do day of registration, there will be a $10 surcharge.  Second race is available for $20 if you want to race multiple categories in a day.

7.  Staging on Saturday will be based on: a.  Cross-Results race predictor. b. Day of registrations
Staging on Sunday will be based on: a.  Top 8 from the series b.  Cross-Results race predictor. c. Day of registrations
All mixed gender junior fields will be staged as follows:  Top 8 (front row) will be 50/50 boys and girls by PMCX series standings (or Cross Results for Race #1).  Rest of field will be mixed according to cross results race predictor.  

Multiple Starts at the same time staging rules: We will be doing 1 minute gaps between fields with the caveat that we reserve the right to combine starts where either or both of them have 10 or less registrants.  In that case, the front row will be split 4/4 and the rest of the field staged by crossresults.com race predictor. 

8.  We will be providing FREE photos to racers.  Look for photographer Bill Kurtz out on course throughout the day. 

9.  Cash Prizes: 

5 or fewer | $85 — $65 — $45

6 racers | $85 — $65 — $45

7 racers | $85 — $65 — $45 — $30

8 racers | $85 — $65 — $45 — $30

9 racers | $85 — $65 — $45 — $30 — $25

10 or more racers | $85 — $65 — $45 — $30 — $25

 

10.  Why are the Open and Womens P123 races different lengths?  Don't you care about equality and equity?  We do.  So much so that we reached out to a handful of elite women to get their opinion, and based on that feedback we made this decision.  Given the constraints of running a whole bunch of categories in the day, and wanting to give women separate time slots from men, what made the most sense for our schedule was to have the P123 women and the 40+ Women share the course and do 50 and 48 minutes respectively, instead of forcing them to race with the men. (we try to make as many people happy as possible.  If you have scheduling suggestions for us that you think would work better, we are always happy to entertain them for next year)

11.  Belltown Throwdown CX, like all Stage 1 Cycling and AirLine Cycles events, is an inclusive race environment that is safe and welcoming to all participants, regardless of sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, race, religion, disability, or ethnic origin. Athletes are allowed to compete in the gender category that they identify as. Non-Binary athletes are welcome to compete in the Non-Binary category or any of the Open and Women categories. 

We strive to create an atmosphere that makes all feel welcome. From Pros to first-time racers, from staff to spectators, we will not accept behavior that is deemed to be bullying or any form of harassment and violators will be asked to leave.  

At any point, if you feel uncomfortable or unsafe or see behavior that seems to be making someone else uncomfortable, please speak to an official or staff member. 

12.  We've tried to get all planning done ahead of time, but sometimes things change for one reason or another (often outside of our control).  Please be understanding and flexible with us.  You can help us put on a great event by REGISTERING EARLY!  We have to plan out porto-potties, food, shirts, porto-potties, registration staff, and even PORTO-LETS based on the expected registration…. so if you always register at the last possible second, you may have time to ponder all life's mysteries as you wait in long porto-let lines!  To help encourage this, the first 50 registrants get a nice discount!

Welcome to Gravel Paradise
Lander, Wyoming—ranked as one of the best outdoor towns in America—is known worldwide for rock climbing and mountain biking, but we’ve been keeping a secret: our gravel is next level. Nestled at the southern tip of the Wind River Range, just west of Jackson and south of the Big Horns, Lander serves up jaw-dropping backdrops, rolling high-desert terrain, and the Popo Agie River flowing right through town.

PLUS: whether or not you are riding, join us for Biketoberfest - a FREE, full day celebration of all things bikes, beer, and community in Lander City Park.

 

 Choose Your Challenge

13-Mile Route: This 13-mile paved cruise is perfect for anyone on a bike looking for an all fun, no pressure ride with family and friends!

 45-Mile Route: Ideal for gravel newbies looking to experience what makes this sport so legendary.

 75-Mile Route: Not quite ready for the full 131? This one gives you a taste of the epic landscape before turning back—just before things get really tough.

 131-Mile Route: The main event. This isn’t just a ride—it’s a true gravel grinder. Expect relentless climbs, rugged terrain, cut-off times, and a real test of endurance. Some won’t finish. Do you have what it takes? (SAG support & bailout points available.)

Your entry fee makes a difference…thus far, The Lance Project Ride 4 Life has raised (and awarded) over $12,000! All proceeds go to scholarships and suicide prevention efforts. Come camp with us! 
This will be a no drop group ride to our private campground at a leasurly pace. Expect mostly gravel roads with some pavement.  Meet at the store at 5pm, we leave at 5:30pm. People generally roll out in the morning at their leasure, but there is usually a small group heading back together. You are welcome to head out by yourself if you'd like. Please don't go in the house without permission. 

Bring food and supplies for the night! Be prepared. 
This event happens rains or shine. 
Kids are welcome with a parent or caretaker. We will be on a busy road for a short distance, please make sure kids know the rules of the road. 

Camp Aberdeen has a lot of space to spread out. It is not recommended to camp next to the fire pit or in the brush. We do our best to control it, but there is a lot of poison ivy on our land. The open fields and paths are generally free of it, but un-cleared places likely have a lot of it.  The lake is swimable, but rinse off afterwards to avoid simmers itch. There is an outdoor shower on the premesis. 

Please leave our campground clean. Pack out what you pack in. There will be a trash can available with limited capacity. 

There is a very large dog named Abel that will bark at you when you arrive. He is harmless, amazing with kids and a big gentle boy. Treat him like you know him and he will lean on you for pets. Ignore him and he will continue to bark. He is loud, but he's a good boy.

EventName: 2026 Rotary Club of Cadillac White Pine Ride
EventNotes:
Rotary Club of Cadillac planning White Pine Ride

CADILLAC — Rotary Club of Cadillac is planning the Eighth Annual White Pine Ride on Saturday, September 12, 2026. The ride attracts more than 100 riders each year. The ride will raise funds for a trail so recognized for its beauty that it was recently ranked among the top 100 Rails-to-Trails in the nation by the Rails-to-Trails Conservancy. Registration includes a t-shirt and picnic lunch with entertainment.

“People can ride independently or in groups and safely while still enjoying this amazing resource right in our community,” said Rotarian Mark Lagerwey. “This is a ride, not a race. Start times are completely voluntary any time all morning on the ride day. ”

Bikers of all ages and skill levels are invited to take part in a 12-, 24-, 58- or 83-mile roundtrip starting from the downtown Cadillac city parking lot located south of the Rotary Performing Arts pavilion. The trail is completely paved and well-maintained by the DNR and Friends of the White Pine Trail.

  • Turtle Pond Family Cruise — 12-mile ride to 48 Road and back

  • Tustin Pleasure Peddler – 24-mile ride to Tustin and back (One gravel culvert crossing)

  • Reed City Ride – 58-mile ride to Reed City and back (one 200-yard gravel section)

  • Tough Enough Tour – 83-mile ride to Big Rapids and back

Riders will be welcomed along the paved trail at rest stops in Hobart, Tustin, Reed City, and Big Rapids. As riders return to Cadillac, a picnic lunch will be provided.

Proceeds from the ride support continued White Pine Trail development and Rotary charities. With proceeds from the first several years the Rotary Club has installed  picnic shelter at the E 44 Road trailhead and is now supporting development of the Ivan Iler arch being installed across the trail in Cadillac. This year's we are also raising funds to install trail crossing safety signs on roads that currently have no warning signs.

“Having the northern trailhead of this nationally ranked trail right in Cadillac has been a great benefit for people from all around Michigan. It's an amazingly beautiful trail, and these historical markers and sculptures will distinguish the trail is a genuine destination for riders, walkers, and others,” Lagerwey added.

Rider registrants will get a free t-shirt and afternoon picnic. Shirts and ride registration packets will be available for pickup at the downtown market Friday evening, September 18, from 6-8 p.m. or the day of the ride September 19 after 7:30 a.m. 

Ride sponsors will have their logos placed on ride shirts and on the White Pine Ride Web site.

For more information and to register for the Rotary Club of Cadillac White Pine Ride, visit: whitepineride.org.

 

For additional information: Mark Lagerwey, 231 357-0851; mwlagerwey@gmail.com

Welcome to Magnolia Gravel Galore Year 9!  We are so excited to do it again with all Ya'll ADVENTURE riders!  Nothing brings joy like a good Gravel ride with friends and some Food, Drinks, and LIVE Music afterwards!  Our new route last year was a Hit, and we plan to do it again!!!!  As usual, we'll continue to add information as we get closer to Race day, and update all riders with necessary details via Emails and social Media.  Hope your having a great 2026, and can't wait to host another Awesome Gravel ride Straight Outta Magnolia!! 

SATUDAY SEPTEMBER 12TH 

All courses will be marked:) Registration opens at 7am.  Rider meeting at 8:45.  9am start!!

57 Mile Course Notes.

Water Spring at Mile 20

Aid Station at the Farm Crossing Mile 26

Aid Station at the Atwood Lake Park mile 40.5

 

We’ll Marshall you out the gravel Lane and head towards downtown Magnolia.  Once we get through the traffic light, the race will start.  You’ll do a short small climb up to state Rt 183 and turn right. From there, we’ll have ½ mile flat straight away to the first GRAVEL section.  I’ll continue to stay in front in a car, and lead out to the first GRAVEL section.   You’ll enter a through Cyclocross gates with ribbon to a doubletrack GRAVEL climb. This will eventually drop down into the sand and Gravel pit area, and then funnel into the abandoned towpath. At the end of the towpath you’ll take a hard right, and head towards the equestrian park.  Once turning into the equestrian park gravel/dirt road, you’ll navigate all the way back until it dead ends into grass section, and then turns left up a challenging narrow path.  This eventually leads you out to your first GRAVEL road, and starts heading to Lake Mohawk.

LAKE MOHAWK

Just before Mohawk, you’ll navigate a cool doubletrack gravel lane around a private property, which is actually a school for special needs kids.  They’re excited to have our route go through the property.  I’ll have information if anyone cares to donate to their cause!! 

Once you enter Mohawk, you’ll have a 1.8 mile pavement section following West Mohawk drive, which turns into East Mohawk dr. You’ll veer onto Sequoya trail for a short climb, and then turn off onto a technical Dirt/Gravel trail.  PLEASE be advised, this trail has a short steep downhill, that needs to be ridden slow, or even walked if you’re newer to the sport. After the short trail section, You’ll start climbing King Rd Gravel, and be off onto Mix Gravel roads until a short jog through the neighborhood of Dellroy.  Shortly after Dellroy, You’ll navigate to the Big Farm Crossing, and the first AID station at mile 26.

 

ATWOOD LAKE

We’ll be Crossing through the Atwood Lake PAVED walking path. It is very scenic and unique. PLEASE USE CAUTION through this section, as it does present some technical turns on GRAVEL.  Signs are indicating when to slow down and be ready for S-curves and using grass corners to eliminate 90 degree turns on GRAVEL.

After Atwood, You’ll climb back into Gravel country, and work your way back to Magnolia and then finish behind the nursey on the gravel lanes through the Evergreens.

PLEASE SAVE MY NUMBER, and USE IT IF NEEDED!

330-904-2650

Aid Station at the Atwood Lake Park mile 18

We’ll Marshall you out the gravel Lane and head towards downtown Magnolia.  Once we get through the traffic light, the race will start.  You’ll do a short small climb up to state Rt 183 and turn right. From there, we’ll have ½ mile flat straight away to the first GRAVEL section.  I’ll continue to stay in front in a car, and lead out to the first GRAVEL section.  You’ll enter a through Cyclocross gates with ribbon to a doubletrack GRAVEL climb. This will eventually drop down into the sand and Gravel pit area, and then funnel into the abandoned towpath. At the end of the towpath you’ll take a hard right, and head towards Gravel Roads and the Atwood Lake region and join up with the longer route until the finish!
